name: 150 mm AGV drive wheel, 48 V
summary: A geared hub motor drive wheel with holding brake and encoder, for warehouse AMRs and factory AGVs. Sample data: the supplier and every figure here are fictional.

demand.reason: India installed a record number of industrial robots in 2024 and factories are automating to meet export quality demands. Mobile robots reorder drive wheels as tread and gears wear.

sources.title: India's robot boom, Association for Advancing Automation
Humanoid robots in 2026 for Indian industry, citing IFR installation figures

notChecked: Any measurement, no sample received yet

parts.name: Hub motor stator
parts.role: Drive the wheel directly from inside the hub.
parts.whatItDoes: A wound stator fixed to the axle. The wheel rim carries the magnets and turns around it.
parts.whyItMatters: Putting the motor in the hub saves space and parts, but the stator then sits where road shock and heat are worst.
parts.material: Silicon steel laminations with copper windings on a steel axle
buyingChecks: Ask for the winding insulation class
Ask for the continuous current at rated load
Check the axle flats and thread match your mount

parts.name: Magnet ring
parts.role: Carry the magnets the stator field pulls around.
parts.whatItDoes: A steel ring with rare-earth magnets bonded inside it, pressed into the wheel rim.
parts.whyItMatters: Magnet grade and bonding decide torque and whether magnets come loose under shock.
buyingChecks: Ask for the magnet grade and maximum temperature
Ask in writing where the magnets are made
Ask how the magnets are retained

parts.name: Wheel rim
parts.role: Carry the tyre and the magnet ring.
parts.whatItDoes: A cast or machined aluminium rim that turns on bearings around the axle.
parts.whyItMatters: Rim stiffness and bearing fit set how true the wheel runs under load.
buyingChecks: Ask for the bearing type and size
Check radial runout on a sample
Ask for the rim alloy

parts.name: Tyre
parts.role: Give grip and carry the load on the floor.
parts.whatItDoes: A polyurethane tread bonded to the rim.
parts.whyItMatters: Tread compound decides grip, floor marking and how fast the wheel wears. It is the most replaced part of a mobile robot.
buyingChecks: Ask for the Shore hardness of the tread
Ask whether the tread is non-marking
Ask whether the tyre can be replaced without a new rim

parts.name: Planetary gearbox
parts.whatItDoes: A compact planetary stage between motor and wheel. Not every hub wheel has one; geared versions carry heavier loads.
parts.whyItMatters: Gear quality sets noise and efficiency. A worn gearbox is the usual source of a robot that starts to whine.
parts.material: Hardened steel gears in an aluminium case
buyingChecks: Ask for the ratio and rated output torque
Ask for the lubricant and service interval
Ask for noise at rated speed

parts.name: Holding brake
parts.role: Hold the robot still when power is off.
parts.whatItDoes: A spring-applied electromagnetic brake. Power releases it, so the wheel locks if power fails.
parts.whyItMatters: On ramps and in e-stops the brake is a safety part. Holding torque must cover the full loaded robot on the steepest slope.
parts.material: Steel armature, friction disc and coil
buyingChecks: Ask for the holding torque and the release voltage
Ask for the brake maker
Check the brake has a manual release for moving a dead robot

parts.name: Encoder
parts.role: Report wheel speed and position to the robot.
parts.whatItDoes: An encoder at the end of the drive, read by the motor controller for odometry and speed control.
parts.whyItMatters: Odometry drift starts here. Resolution and mounting play both add up over a long route.
parts.material: Magnetic or optical encoder in a plastic cap
buyingChecks: Ask for the encoder resolution
Ask for the output type: incremental, absolute or Hall only
Ask for the cable and connector type

parts.name: Mounting bracket
parts.role: Fix the drive wheel to the robot chassis.
parts.whatItDoes: A steel bracket that clamps the fixed axle and bolts to the chassis or a suspension arm.
parts.whyItMatters: The bracket carries the full robot load and every bump. Its fit decides whether the wheel stays aligned.
buyingChecks: Check the bolt pattern against your chassis
Ask for the rated static load
Ask whether a suspension version is available
